$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for 1P/2P/3P logo usage. Documents how each logo tier is rendered (bare vs. bordered tile vs. borderless-in-tile). Human-readable rationale lives in logo-usage.ts. The threeP.borderlessIds list MUST mirror /public/3p folders that ship a 16-borderless.svg (enforced by logo-usage.source.test.js).

oneP.description: Atlassian product marks from @atlaskit/logo. Most ship a solid superellipse background, so they render bare. The Atlassian master logo has no solid background and needs a bordered tile.

twoP.description: Marketplace partner logos at /public/2p/<vendor>.png. Bare PNG marks with no background, so they always need a bordered containing tile.

threeP.description: Third-party marks at /public/3p/<id>/<size>.svg. Solid-fill marks paint their own background and render bare. White-tile marks ship a 16-borderless.svg sibling: render the borderless glyph inside a VPK-drawn bordered tile so borders don't double up. Transparent-glyph marks ship no borderless sibling but still need a tile — list those in borderedIds.
threeP.$insetScaleComment: Optional per-id inset: the glyph renders at size*scale, centered in the full size box, so a full-bleed mark can sit inset with padding (e.g. VS Code at 20px inside a 24px box = 20/24). Defaults to 1 (no inset).
threeP.$darkGlyphIdsComment: Marks whose glyph is monochrome near-black, so they vanish on a dark backdrop (e.g. GitHub #1d2022 scores 1.0:1 against --ds-surface #1F1F21; WCAG non-text wants 3:1). Consumers that place a bare glyph on a themed surface invert these in dark mode. DERIVED, not hand-written: an id belongs here when every fill in its package entrypoint (or /public/3p/<id>/24.svg) scores below 1.5:1 against the dark surface. logo-usage.source.test.js recomputes this from the shipped markup, so a package upgrade that recolors a mark fails the build instead of silently regressing contrast. Genuinely colored dark marks (Datadog purple, Box blue) are excluded on purpose — inverting them would corrupt the brand hue.
threeP.$borderedIdsComment: Transparent-glyph marks that paint no background and ship no 16-borderless.svg sibling. They still need a bordered tile, rendered from the base <size>.svg with no variant swap. MUST stay disjoint from borderlessIds (checked first). An id belongs here only while no upstream @atlassian/logo-third-party entrypoint exists — prefer wiring packageIcon in logo-third-party-data.ts, which gets the border from the package tile.
